name: MonarchReactionBar
title: ReactionBar
wrapsNative: MonarchFlowLayout (a SwiftUI Layout) of Button chips with AccessibilityTraits.isToggle and .isSelected; Button with sheet(isPresented:) holding MonarchEmojiPicker
summary: The emoji reactions under a message, comment or post: a chip per emoji with its count, selected when you reacted, and a button that opens the emoji picker.
whenToUse: Under messages, comments and posts where people react with emoji.
whenNotToUse: Not for filters or selectable labels; use MonarchTag. Not for a single like button; use a Toggle with MonarchToggleButtonStyle.
api: init(_ reactions: [MonarchReactionBarItem], size: MonarchReactionBarSize = .sm, maxReactions: Int? = nil, isAddable: Bool = true, quickReactions: [String] = [], labels: MonarchReactionBarLabels = MonarchReactionBarLabels(), onToggle: (@MainActor (String, Bool) -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchReactionBarItem.init(_ emoji: String, count: Int, isReacted: Bool = false, label: String? = nil, reactedBy: String? = nil)

MonarchReactionBarLabels.init(label: String? = nil, reaction: (@Sendable (String, Int) -> String)? = nil, add: String? = nil, reactedBy: String? = nil, picker: MonarchEmojiPickerLabels = MonarchEmojiPickerLabels())

options.name: reactions
options.description: The reactions in display order. A count of 0 hides the chip; a repeated emoji is shown once.

options.name: size
options.description: sm under messages and comments, md under posts.

options.name: maxReactions
options.description: At most this many distinct reactions; the add button hides when the limit is reached.

options.name: isAddable
options.description: Whether an interactive bar shows the add button.

options.name: quickReactions
options.description: Emoji offered first in the picker, as its recents row.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the bar's name, a chip's name, the add button, the "Reacted by" heading and the picker's strings.

options.name: onToggle
options.description: Receives the emoji and the new state when a chip is tapped, or true when an emoji is picked. Without it the bar is read-only.

states.name: not reacted
states.description: A chip on the subtle background with a thin border and the count in regular weight.

states.name: reacted
states.description: A chip in the accent's subtle fill and strong text, a 2-point accent border and a bold count; the chip has the selected trait.

states.name: read-only
states.description: Chips are images, not buttons, with no add button; nothing is drawn without reactions.

states.name: picker open
states.description: The emoji picker in a sheet at medium height; picking closes it.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Chips and the add button use the disabled text colour and do not respond.

appearance: Capsule chips on the subtle background with the subtle border, or in the accent's subtle fill, strong text and border when reacted; the add button in the muted text colour. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web bar is a toolbar with one tab stop and arrow keys between chips; on iOS each chip is a button VoiceOver reaches by swiping, and full keyboard access moves between them with Tab. The web opens the picker in a popover; iOS opens it in a sheet at medium height, which iPad shows as a form sheet. Who reacted is VoiceOver's more content and the pointer hover text instead of a title attribute. A chip's default spoken name comes from the emoji picker's built-in English index when no label is given.
accessibility: The bar is a container named "Reactions".
Each chip is a button with the toggle trait, named by the emoji's name and count, "thumbs up, 3 reactions"; the emoji character itself is not read.
A reacted chip has the selected trait, and a thicker border and bold count, so the state does not depend on colour.
Who reacted is offered as VoiceOver more content under "Reacted by".
Chips are at least 44 points wide and their touch targets 44 points high; the add button is 44 by 44 points and named "Add reaction".
Read-only chips are images with the same names.
Text scales with Dynamic Type and chips wrap onto new rows.
edgeCases: Taking back the last reaction of an emoji removes its chip when the product updates reactions.
Picking an emoji you already reacted with does not call onToggle.
Large counts are formatted with the locale's grouping, such as 1,204.
An emoji that is not in the built-in index is read by its character unless a label is given.
